### Introduction:

This exercise may seem a little bit strange, but keep doing it.

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

### Step 2. Import the dataset from this [address](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/iris/iris.data).

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable called iris

```{r}
url <- "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/iris/iris.data"

# the file has no header row: col_names = FALSE keeps the first row as data
iris <- read_csv(url, col_names = FALSE)

head(iris)
```

### Step 4. Create columns for the dataset

The columns are:

1. sepal_length (in cm)
2. sepal_width (in cm)
3. petal_length (in cm)
4. petal_width (in cm)
5. class

```{r}
names(iris) <- c("sepal_length", "sepal_width", "petal_length", "petal_width", "class")
head(iris)
```

### Step 5. Is there any missing value in the dataframe?

```{r}
colSums(is.na(iris))
# nice no missing value
```

### Step 6. Lets set the values of the rows 10 to 29 of the column 'petal_length' to NA

```{r}
# pandas counts rows from 0, so its rows 10 to 29 are rows 11 to 30 in R
iris$petal_length[11:30] <- NA
head(iris, 20)
```

### Step 7. Good, now lets substitute the NA values to 1.0

```{r}
iris <- iris |> mutate(petal_length = replace_na(petal_length, 1))
iris
```

### Step 8. Now let's delete the column class

```{r}
iris <- iris |> select(-class)
head(iris)
```

### Step 9. Set the first 3 rows as NA

```{r}
iris[1:3, ] <- NA
head(iris)
```

### Step 10. Delete the rows that have NA

```{r}
iris <- iris |> drop_na()
head(iris)
```

### Step 11. Reset the index so it begins with 1 again

```{r}
# tibbles are always numbered from 1 to n, so there is nothing to reset.
# With a base data.frame you would use: rownames(iris) <- NULL
head(iris)
```
